metadata.title: The Universe You Can Afford.
metadata.clock: narration (Kokoro af_bella) - per-beat mp3 durations are MEASURED, never estimated
metadata.greeting_note: hello lexicon: Hindi (Namaste). Ep. 03 Hej, Ep. 04 Ciao, Ep. 05 Ola, Ep. 06 Salut; no language repeats within the series.
metadata.target_runtime: Under 3:00 BY DESIGN. The human asked for under three minutes on Ep. 06 after a 5:23 first cut, so this episode was WRITTEN to a word budget derived from Ep. 06's measured speech rate (0.3843 s/word) rather than trimmed afterwards. Predicted 2:51.
metadata.purpose: Ep. 07 of the AI in Astronomy & Space Science series, from weekly_stem_videos/ideas.md Astronomy topic 07 (Simulating the universe - AI-accelerated cosmological simulations replacing expensive N-body calculations).
metadata.color_semantics: Claude fidelity palette. Terracotta #D97757 is the ONE accent and marks THE CHEAP ANSWER throughout - the Zel'dovich curve, the Zel'dovich panel, the approximation's error. Ink marks the expensive truth. That mapping is fixed for the whole reel so the viewer never re-learns which is which. Cosmic-web plates are bright-on-dark warm monochrome; the one line plot is ink-on-white.
metadata.distinct_from_earlier_episodes: Eps. 01-06 all had AI looking at OBSERVATIONS - triaging, classifying, detecting, deciding. Ep. 07 is the first where there is nothing to look at: you cannot run an experiment on the universe, so a theory's only voice is a simulation, and the AI's job is to STAND IN FOR THE PHYSICS rather than inspect data. The limit is correspondingly new - the emulator is trained on N-body output, so it is a compression of simulations already paid for and cannot be trusted outside that box. That is a circularity, not an accuracy ceiling (Ep. 04), an unseen class (Ep. 03), an irreversible rejection (Ep. 05) or a latency (Ep. 06).
metadata.note: ILLUSTRATE LAW: the Claude UI appears at B00, B11, B12, B13. Every other beat illustrates its concept as a reel-local Manim scene (scenes.py). All plates are generated by assets/gen_cosmos.py, which ACTUALLY RUNS both calculations the episode describes - a Zel'dovich displacement and a particle-mesh N-body solve in 2D - so the comparison on screen is a measured result, not an illustration. Every beat showing a plate captions it as a 2D toy at 512^2. No LaTeX/MathTex anywhere. metadata.channel_title is omitted for the GATE V edge-bleed reason logged in Ep. 03. scenes.py is ASPECT-AWARE: one file lays out 16:9 and the 9:16 derivative in short/.
